subject: Run ectotherm with micro_terra or replace micro_global climate base

messages.author: 7b9976a7166ab661
messages.subject: Run ectotherm with micro_terra or replace micro_global climate base
parts:
Hello, good day to everyone.

--I am using the ectotherm function in NicheMapR with the dynamic energy budget (DEB) parameter enabled to predict activity, morphology, and demographic variables of a tropical sceloporine lizard. My study is framed in various geographical points during three successive months of a particular year (2017). 
--I know that I must use micro_global to predict the microclimate used by ecototherm for its calculations, and that I can extract from the predictions the data corresponding to the months and hours of interest. 
--However, I need to be able to specify the year in question, not a number of years from the climate database that micro_global handles by default. I can specify the year and months with micro_ncep, but I have not been able to run ectotherm with DEB=1 using micro_ncep. I think I could use micro_terra for that task because it has the nyear parameter, but I'm not sure.

I have two questions, first, which NicheMapR microclimatic function (where I can specify a particular year) can I concatenate with the ectotherm function (with parameter DEB=1) to obtain morphological (mass) and demographic (intrinsic rate of natural increase) variables.
Second, if this cannot be done with micro_terra, is there a tutorial where I can learn how to replace the micro_global climatic database with another corresponding to the year 2017?

Thank you very much in advance for your time and interest.

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Run ectotherm with micro_terra or replace micro_global climate base
parts:
Hi Israel,

There should be no problem running the ectotherm model, with or without the DEB model, from any of the microclimate functions. What is going wrong for you when you try? If you can share a simple example producing the problem, I can hopefully see what the problem is.

Also, what species of lizard are you studying? Have you estimated DEB parameters for it?

All the best,
Mike

Hello, thank you for your answer, it helped me to clarify and move forward. For some reason I couldn't concatenate micro_ncep with ecotherm but that is no longer the case.

That was a necessary step because I am interested in calculating the mass and intrinsic rate of natural growth of adult lizards during the hottest quarter (March 1 to May 30) of 2017 at my study site (in Morelos, Mexico; e.g., -99.19706,18.45588). But, although I set the initial stage at the reproductive adult stage (stage <- 3), the ectotherm function starts calculations from the juvenile stage (stage <- 2), which can be seen in the figure to be generated (at the end of the script). This caused the debout WETMASS variables to throw me values of mass corresponding to juveniles (from 7.6g) when I had defined a higher average mass corresponding to adults (Ww_g= 36).
I am interested then that the ectotherm begins with the calculations from the adult stage.

* Also, when running the period between 2016-01-02 to 2018-12-30, I expected the mass increase curve to stop at 36g, but instead it kept changing
up to 51.7g. I don't understand why that would happen.

* If the calculations could not be started in the reproductive adult stage, I thought of setting a period of 5 years (average age of Sceloporina lizards) in which the lizard would mature to its reproductive age, but continuously exposing the lizard to the climatic conditions of the
hottest quarter of 2017, meaning that the quarter was repeated 20 times. I don't know if it's possible or how to achieve it.

* If the previous point were possible, I have found the problem that when I spread the period beyond 2017 (820 days from 2016-03-01 to 2018-05-30) and change the days and months of the vignette of micro_ncep (364 days from 2017-01-02 to 2017-12-30), the program gives me the

even when maxshades has the same number of elements as the number of simulated days.
There is no problem if I change the days and months within 2017 (92 days from 2017-03-01 to 2017-05-30) or if I keep the days and months of the  vignette although the years vary (1094 days from 2016-01-02 to 2018-12-30).

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Run ectotherm with micro_terra or replace micro_global climate base
parts:
Hi Israel,

When you turn the DEB model on, the Ww_g parameter no longer specifies the weight - it is driven by the DEB model and its parameters (in your case, for Eulamprus quoyii). You started the model at 'puberty'. This is not maximum size but when the lizard is mature which means it's started to allocate to reproduction. So it grows from 12 g to the maximum size of ~50 g. But note that debout$WETMASS is including reproduction buffer (and stomach contents), and the sudden drops were it laying a clutch.  If you want it to start at the maximum size, you need to specify the initial structure as L.m^3 not L.p^3 (i.e., maximum length cubed, not length at puberty cubed).

Re the shade - yes you need to make sure it's a vector of the same number of days as the microclimate output. You can just not specify it in the call to 'ectotherm' if you want to make it the same as what the microclimate model was run at, because by default it takes micro$MINSHADES and micro$MAXSHADES as input. I had no problem running it for the different date ranges. Just try without specifying minshade and maxshade and it should work, then you can debug what's going wrong from there if you're still having trouble specifying shade manually.

Also, note that in the current version the DEB parameter input F.m should now be p.Xm, i.e., replace
F_m=F.m
with
p_Xm = p.Xm
in the call to the ectotherm model.

Note that the ectotherm model expects microclimate input in a particular format, but you can overwrite that with whatever you want and make manually constructed versions e.g. of metout, shadmet etc. You just have to be careful to keep the same number of days/hours for each input variable or else the program will crash due to memory problems.

All the best,
Mike

El mar, 6 sept 2022 a las 0:51, NicheMapR (<nich...@googlegroups.com>) escribió:

Hi Israel,

When you turn the DEB model on, the Ww_g parameter no longer specifies the weight - it is driven by the DEB model and its parameters (in your case, for Eulamprus quoyii). You started the model at 'puberty'. This is not maximum size but when the lizard is mature which means it's started to allocate to reproduction. So it grows from 12 g to the maximum size of ~50 g. But note that debout$WETMASS is including reproduction buffer (and stomach contents), and the sudden drops were it laying a clutch.  If you want it to start at the maximum size, you need to specify the initial structure as L.m^3 not L.p^3 (i.e., maximum length cubed, not length at puberty cubed).

Re the shade - yes you need to make sure it's a vector of the same number of days as the microclimate output. You can just not specify it in the call to 'ectotherm' if you want to make it the same as what the microclimate model was run at, because by default it takes micro$MINSHADES and micro$MAXSHADES as input. I had no problem running it for the different date ranges. Just try without specifying minshade and maxshade and it should work, then you can debug what's going wrong from there if you're still having trouble specifying shade manually.

Also, note that in the current version the DEB parameter input F.m should now be p.Xm, i.e., replace
F_m=F.m
with
p_Xm = p.Xm
in the call to the ectotherm model.

Note that the ectotherm model expects microclimate input in a particular format, but you can overwrite that with whatever you want and make manually constructed versions e.g. of metout, shadmet etc. You just have to be careful to keep the same number of days/hours for each input variable or else the program will crash due to memory problems.

All the best,
Mike
